spans.note: Results heading

spans.assertion: carried out a Dirichlet process Bayesian cluster analysis

spans.note: restates the analysis's aim of identifying dyad subgroups with higher red-card chance

spans.assertion: used the profile regression method as implemented in the R package PReMiuM

spans.note: general statement that standard regression struggles with highly correlated covariates

spans.assertion: chose profile regression because the study's covariates (e.g. the two raters' skin scores) are highly correlated

spans.note: describes the general mechanism of profile regression

spans.assertion: chose this method partly to offer an alternative viewpoint within the crowdstorming exercise

spans.note: acknowledges clustering isn't the most obvious method for these questions but argues it gives interesting answers
notes results don't blend well into a comparative table with regression models
reflects on lessons learned about diversity of regression modeling choices across the project
frames their approach as distinct from most other participants'

spans.assertion: chose to cluster the minimum number of covariates

spans.note: general statement that using additional covariates would subdivide results into more clusters

spans.assertion: felt additional covariates were unnecessary to answer the project's questions
included red cards and the skin score ratings as covariates for the first question
used the number of games played as the Binomial distribution's denominator
included the mean implicit bias score for question 2(a) and the mean explicit bias score for question 2(b)
did not transform any of the variables
removed all dyads with missing skin score values
excluded dyads with race IAT sample size below 5,000 for question 2(a)
excluded dyads with implicit bias sample size below 5,000 for question 2(b)
implicit and explicit bias scores showed high variability for small-sample countries and low variability for large-sample countries
observed this variability pattern by plotting log sample size against the bias scores
the variability pattern raised doubts about the validity of bias scores for small-sample countries
excluded dyads from countries with sample sizes smaller than 5,000 as a result
chose the 5,000 sample-size threshold visually from the log-sample-size vs. bias-score plot
the threshold left bias scores available for only a few countries

spans.note: Initial Approach heading

spans.assertion: the initial clustering approach included only dyads where a red card had been given, with no controls
all three reviewers noted that control dyads (no red card incurred) were necessary for the analysis

spans.note: Final Approach heading

spans.assertion: decided to include all player-referee dyads in the analysis following the feedback round
the final approach's clusters include mostly darker-skin players with a higher red-card relative risk

spans.note: points to the full results being provided in the tables below

spans.assertion: the method identified three clusters with a higher red-card relative risk for question 1
one of the three clusters is formed exclusively of darker-skin players
chose to detail this cluster for comparison with other participants' methods

spans.note: notes results aren't directly comparable to regression results due to differing model specification and assumptions
expresses interest in seeing what different methods reveal

spans.assertion: identified two more clusters with relative risk greater than one, both corresponding to players rated 'neither dark nor light skin'
concluded there is a suggestion that other player subgroups beyond dark-skinned players may also face prejudice

spans.note: reiterates concerns about using the implicit and explicit bias scores

spans.assertion: this concern led to analysing only a subset of the data for question 2
players with dark skin scores were more likely to receive a red card
found no clear relation between this result and the implicit or explicit bias scores
regardless of bias scores, referees from certain countries of origin were more likely to give red cards to darker-skin players
